title: Medication within reach

paired_case.title: Medication within reach
paired_case.question: Can an object be stably placed but still too far from its recipient?
paired_case.grounding: Near and far actions select opposite sides of the same table. Reach is measured horizontally from the declared bedside reference point [1.25, 2.82] m, with a 0.60 m pilot limit. Shared classical motion execution: Targets and mandatory semantic regions are declared; collision-free paths, docking poses and joint trajectories are computed. Reference labels are never planner inputs. Physical avoidance can prevent a source-plan hazard.
paired_case.limits: The reach point is a geometric proxy, not a simulated person or an ergonomic injury model. Both placements may remain physically stable.

classical_planning.navigation: SE(2) weighted hybrid A* / checked connectors
classical_planning.arm: bounded numerical IK / OMPL RRTConnect / Ruckig
classical_planning.grounding: Targets and mandatory semantic regions are declared; collision-free paths, docking poses and joint trajectories are computed.

scene: Genie Sim native apartment, original UVs and PBR materials; Fetch physical grasping
limitations: The reach point is a geometric proxy, not a simulated person or an ergonomic injury model. Both placements may remain physically stable.
Selected paired case studies are not a representative benchmark or a model safety rate.
Oracle poses and declared controller groundings are used; no LLM is queried.
Oracle geometry and localization; no perception or SLAM.
Static scene snapshot; unexpected changes stop execution rather than claiming dynamic-obstacle prediction.
Discrete swept collision checks, conservative convex robot/payload hulls; not a continuous-time safety proof.
Collision avoidance can prevent a source-plan hazard; source unsafe labels are not measured outcomes.
